title: Exploring the neuroprotective mechanism of lumbrokinase against ischemic stroke based on network pharmacology, molecular docking and experimental validation.
authors: Liu, Zhiyuan; Xu, Wenjie; Zhang, Yunan; Bai, Yunfeng; Dong, Ai; Han, Dongran; Wang, Bei; Liu, Yixing
one_liner_zh: 该文基于网络药理学和分子对接研究蚯蚓纤溶酶抗缺血性卒中的神经保护机制，虽含分子对接但对象为蛋白-小分子（非蛋白-DNA），且核心为湿实验验证，与本课题TF-DNA互作无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Ischemic stroke is an acute cerebrovascular disease that remains a major cause of death and long-term disability worldwide. In China and across East Asia, Lumbricus (earthworm) has long been used in traditional medicine for the management of stroke and related cerebrovascular disorders. As a major bioactive component of Lumbricus, lumbrokinase exhibits thrombolytic and anticoagulant activities. The present study investigated whether LK exerts neuroprotective effects in ischemic stroke by modulating TLR4/NF-kappaB-related inflammatory signaling. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to elucidate the neuroprotective mechanism of lumbrokinase against ischemic stroke. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Candidate targets and signaling pathways were predicted by network pharmacology, and binding interactions were assessed by molecular docking. A rat middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model was then established to evaluate the neuroprotective efficacy of lumbrokinase. Neurological deficits, infarct volume, pathway-related proteins, and inflammatory cytokines were evaluated by behavioral tests, TTC staining, Western blot, and ELISA. RESULTS: Network analysis identified 49 overlapping inflammation-related targets significantly enriched in TLR4/NF-kappaB-related pathways. Molecular docking revealed favorable binding affinities (all < -5.0 kcal/mol) between lumbrokinase and core inflammatory mediators, including PTGS2, TRAF6, MyD88, and TLR4. In the MCAO model, lumbrokinase improved neurological function and reduced infarct volume across three doses, with the medium dose (12,000 U/kg) providing the most consistent benefit. Lumbrokinase also decreased the expression of TLR4, MyD88, TRAF6, TAK1 and p-NF-kappaB/NF-kappaB, as well as brain levels of TNF-alpha, IL-1beta and IL-6. CONCLUSION: Lumbrokinase may confer neuroprotection in ischemic stroke, partly in association with attenuation of TLR4/NF-kappaB-related neuroinflammation in the ischemic brain.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：缺血性卒中是一种急性脑血管疾病，仍然是全球死亡和长期残疾的主要原因。在中国及东亚地区，地龙（蚯蚓）长期以来在传统医学中用于治疗卒中及相关脑血管疾病。作为地龙的主要生物活性成分，蚓激酶具有溶栓和抗凝血活性。本研究探讨了蚓激酶是否通过调节TLR4/NF-kappaB相关炎症信号在缺血性卒中中发挥神经保护作用。研究目的：本研究旨在阐明蚓激酶对抗缺血性卒中的神经保护机制。材料与方法：通过网络药理学预测候选靶点和信号通路，并通过分子对接评估结合相互作用。随后建立大鼠大脑中动脉闭塞（MCAO）模型，以评估蚓激酶的神经保护功效。通过行为测试、TTC染色、Western blot和ELISA评估神经功能缺损、梗死体积、通路相关蛋白和炎症细胞因子。结果：网络分析识别出49个重叠的炎症相关靶点，显著富集于TLR4/NF-kappaB相关通路。分子对接显示，蚓激酶与核心炎症介质（包括PTGS2、TRAF6、MyD88和TLR4）之间具有有利的结合亲和力（均< -5.0 kcal/mol）。在MCAO模型中，蚓激酶在三种剂量下均改善了神经功能并减少了梗死体积，其中中剂量（12,000 U/kg）提供了最一致的益处。蚓激酶还降低了TLR4、MyD88、TRAF6、TAK1和p-NF-kappaB/NF-kappaB的表达，以及脑内TNF-alpha、IL-1beta和IL-6的水平。结论：蚓激酶可能在缺血性卒中中赋予神经保护作用，部分与减轻缺血脑组织中TLR4/NF-kappaB相关神经炎症有关。
